### Architecture Decisions

| Requirement | Solution |
|---|---|
| Fast first load | Server-side prerendering (default with `blazor` template) |
| Snappy after load, no round-trips | **Interactive WebAssembly** render mode — runs in browser |
| Worldwide users / latency | WebAssembly runs locally after download; no SignalR needed |
| Interactive controls on every page | `@rendermode InteractiveWebAssembly` on all pages |
| Individual accounts auth | ASP.NET Core Identity with SQLite + cookie auth |

### Key Files

- **Server API**: `ShipmentTracker/Endpoints/ShipmentEndpoints.cs` — CRUD endpoints for shipments
- **Dispatcher page**: `ShipmentTracker.Client/Pages/Shipments.razor` — list, filter, update status, create shipments (requires auth)
- **Customer page**: `ShipmentTracker.Client/Pages/Track.razor` — public tracking by number with progress bar
- **Seed data**: 5 sample shipments pre-populated on first run
- **DB**: SQLite with EF Core migrations

### Run

```bash
cd ShipmentTracker/ShipmentTracker
dotnet run
```

Register an account, then access the Dispatcher dashboard. The Track page is available without login.
